decisions.reason: We keep the dietary supplement range because it is a visible portfolio-expansion project aligned with our announced consumer-health growth path, making reversal harder to justify after the initial launch investment.

We keep the skin and hair supplement because it received a dedicated launch and standalone presentation early on, so management is inclined to continue a publicly committed consumer-health extension rather than concede a false start.
We drop the joint health supplement because it showed the weakest initial visibility and comparatively limited commitment, making it the easiest low-sunk-cost line extension to exit.

We keep the mushroom-based immune supplement because it was publicly promoted as an innovative new addition to the range, and any disappointing performance can still be explained as temporary market timing rather than a fundamental error.

We keep the generic blood pressure medication because it embodies substantial regulatory and manufacturing investment, and the valsartan issue can be treated as a temporary external quality shock rather than a reason to abandon the product.

We keep the over-the-counter migraine triptan because it supports the stated broadening of the portfolio and likely required meaningful launch and regulatory effort, so management would persist without clear evidence of lasting failure.
